Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Kumar Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State-respondent and Sri Pradeep Kumar Shukla learned counsel who has filed vakalatnama on behalf of the complainant which is taken on record.
The instant application has been moved seeking bail in respect of Case Crime No.364 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304-B, 201 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act Police Station Dhanepur, District Gonda during trial.

sentences.text: The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
As per the version contained in the FIR, it is alleged that the complainant who is the brother of the deceased had married his sister with Sri Pawan Verma the co-accused in the year, 2018.
It is further stated that the family members of the co-accused Pawan Verma (husband of the deceased) used to trouble the deceased for want of adequate dowry.
They tried to pressurize the deceased for getting a four wheeler and since the deceased could not comply with the said demand she was subjected to harassment and cruelty both physically and mentally.

It is in this context that the complainant is said to have received information on 27.11.2023 that the applicant along with all other co-accused had been instrumental in killing the deceased and, thereafter, the body was hidden near visuhi river.
Further submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is married sister-in-law (Nanand) of the deceased.
It is further submitted that the complainant unmindfully implicated all the relatives including the applicant.
It is further stated that at the time of lodging of the FIR, it was clearly indicated by the complainant that the dead body was hidden near river bank of Visuhi.

Thus,
this statement belies the version of the prosecution that on the pointing of the applicant, the dead body was recovered, as the complainant at the time of lodging the FIR already know about the body.
It is further urged that there has been no demand made by the applicant nor she could be said to reap any benefit even if the four wheeler would have been given.
The applicant is a resident of different village after her marriage.
She is also having two minor children and moreso, she was not present on the spot on the date of incident.

In the aforesaid circumstances, where the applicant does not have any criminal history and has stable matrimonial family background living in different village yet she has been in jail since 29.11.2023.
It is also urged that in the aforesaid circumstances the applicant neither can influence any witnesses or tamper with any evidence.
Charge sheet has been filed.
There is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released on bail or tampering with the witnesses.

In case,
the applicant is enlarged on bail, she shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
The co-accused Ram Preet (Nandoi of the deceased) has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 03.05.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application no.4815 of 2024.

sentences.text: Learned AGA as well as counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application and there is nothing on record, at this stage, that could indicate as to how the complainant received the information regarding the dead body being hidden on the banks of the river Visuhi.

Considering the rival submissions as well as the facts and circumstances of the case and the material available on record also considering the nature of allegations and accusation against the applicant,
the severity of the punishment if convicted and the period of incarceration as well as the fact that no apprehension has been expressed by the learned AGA that the applicant is at the risk of fleeing justice or that he would tamper with evidence or influence any witness, hence, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant is Sitapati vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P. ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142122800/
2 entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the instant bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Sitapati involved in the above-mentioned case crime be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond with two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

sentences.text:
At the time of executing required sureties, the following conditions shall be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through her counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(iv) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the trial court, absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
